Topic: The Origin and Color Dependence of the Index of Refraction

Target audience: Undergraduate Physics/Engineering Students

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite: The Harmonic Oscillator Model

Lecture lines:
Electrons act like masses on springs.
[Asset: LorentzOscillatorModel] shows driving force.
Light wave pushes electrons to oscillate.

Planned animations:
Display a spring-mass system with label '#FFFFFF' mass and '#FFD700' spring.
Oscillate the mass horizontally; change label color to '#00FFFF' to signify movement.
Fade in a sine wave graph tracking the mass displacement.
Highlight the equilibrium point with a pulsing '#FF00FF' circle.
Animate the wave frequency increasing; mass oscillates faster.

Section: section_2 — Origin: Light-Matter Interaction

Lecture lines:
Electrons emit secondary waves.
These waves lag behind incident light.
[Asset: WaveInterferenceAnimation] creates resultant wave.
This interaction slows phase velocity.
Phase lag produces index refraction.

Planned animations:
Display an incoming light wave (sinusoidal) as an oscillating vector.
Show the light wave entering a dense atomic medium.
Animate the electron oscillation reacting to the light wave field.
Show the electron emitting a secondary spherical re-radiation wave.
Illustrate the interference of the incident and re-radiated waves.

Section: section_3 — Mechanism: Color Dependence (Dispersion)

Lecture lines:
Atoms have natural resonance frequency.
[Asset: DispersionGraph] shows frequency dependence.
Phase lag shifts near resonance.
Index varies with light color.
Blue light bends more intensely.

Planned animations:
Show atoms with varying natural electron resonant frequencies.
Animate incident waves of low, medium, and high frequencies.
Highlight electrons oscillating with amplitude dependent on frequency.

Section: section_4 — Visualizing Dispersion: The Rainbow Effect

Lecture lines:
Prisms show color-dependent bending.
[Asset: RainbowPrismAnimation] splits spectrum.
Different colors follow unique paths.

Planned animations:
Display a white light beam entering a triangular glass prism.
Show the beam splitting into constituent colors (ROYGBIV) inside.
Flash the varying refraction angles for each color output.

Section: section_5 — Real-World Application: Chromatic Aberration

Lecture lines:
Lenses focus colors at differences.
[Asset: ChromaticAberrationAnimation] causes blur.
Achromatic doublets correct color fringes.

Planned animations:
Show a camera lens focusing white light onto a sensor.
Display color fringing around edges due to dispersion.
Highlight the sensor plane with blurred overlapping color spots.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Lenses focus colors at differences.",
            "Chromatic aberration causes blur.",
            "Achromatic doublets correct color fringes."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: Chromatic Aberration", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup visual elements
        lens = Ellipse(width=1.0, height=3.0, color='#ADD8E6', fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(lens, 'C2')
        
        # Rays
        ray_blue = Line(start=[-3, 1, 0], end=self.grid['C2'], color='#0000FF')
        ray_red = Line(start=[-3, -1, 0], end=self.grid['C2'], color='#FF0000')
        
        # Focus points
        focus_blue = Dot(color='#0000FF').move_to(self.grid['C4'])
        focus_red = Dot(color='#FF0000').move_to(self.grid['C5'])
        
        # Blurred sensor area
        sensor = Rectangle(width=0.2, height=2.0, color='#FFFFFF', fill_opacity=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(sensor, 'C4')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color('#FFFF00')
        self.play(Create(lens), Create(ray_blue), Create(ray_red))
        self.play(
            FadeIn(focus_blue),
            FadeIn(focus_red)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color('#FFFF00')
        self.play(FadeIn(sensor))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color('#FFFF00')
        # Simulate correction
        self.play(
            focus_blue.animate.move_to(focus_red.get_center()),
            sensor.animate.move_to(focus_red.get_center())
        )
        self.wait(2)
